source.name: Canonical upper ontology with historical physical projection
source.overlayPolicy: Use the project canonical Entity/Object/Property/Relation projection while retaining the historical physical descendants.

nodes.label: Abstract entity
nodes.definition: An entity whose identity does not depend on one particular physical embodiment.

nodes.label: Adjective
nodes.definition: One of the parts of speech. The &%Class of &%Words that conventionally denote &%Attributes of &%Objects.

nodes.label: Adverb
nodes.definition: One of the parts of speech. The &%Class of &%Words that conventionally denote &%Attributes of &%Processes.

nodes.label: Age Group
nodes.definition: A &%GroupOfPeople whose &%members all have the same &%age.

nodes.label: Agreement
nodes.definition: A shared commitment or alignment between participants.

nodes.label: Alga
nodes.definition: A chiefly aquatic plant that contains chlorophyll, but does not form embryos during development and lacks vascular tissue.

nodes.label: Algebraic entity
nodes.definition: An entity defined through algebraic operations or laws.

nodes.label: Algorithm
nodes.definition: A finite, effective procedure for producing a result.

nodes.label: Amphibian
nodes.definition: A cold-blooded, smooth-skinned &%Vertebrate which characteristically hatches as an aquatic larva, breathing by gills. When mature, the &%Amphibian breathes with &%Lungs.

nodes.label: Analytic entity
nodes.definition: An entity defined through limits, variation, or analytic operations.

nodes.label: Anatomical Structure
nodes.definition: A normal or pathological part of the anatomy or structural organization of an &%Organism. This class covers &%BodyParts, as well as structures that are given off by &%Organisms, e.g. &%ReproductiveBodies.

nodes.label: Animal
nodes.definition: An &%Organism with eukaryotic &%Cells, and lacking stiff cell walls, plastids, and photosynthetic pigments.

nodes.label: Animal Language
nodes.definition: The &%subclass of &%Languages used by &%Animals other than &%Humans.

nodes.label: Ape
nodes.definition: Various &%Primates with no tails or only short tails.

nodes.label: Aquatic Mammal
nodes.definition: The &%Class of &%Mammals that dwell chiefly in the water. Includes whales, dolphins, manatees, seals, and walruses.

nodes.label: Art Work
nodes.definition: &%Artifacts that are created primarily for aesthetic appreciation. Note that this &%Class does not include most examples of architecture, which belong under &%StationaryArtifact.

nodes.label: Article
nodes.definition: A relatively short &%Text that either is unbound or is bound with other &%Articles in a &%Book.

nodes.label: Artifact
nodes.definition: An &%Object that is the product of a &%Making.

nodes.label: Astronomical Body
nodes.definition: The &%Class of all astronomical objects of significant size. It includes &%SelfConnectedObjects like planets, stars, and asteroids, as well as &%Collections like nebulae, galaxies, and constellations. Note that the planet Earth is an &%AstronomicalBody, but every &%Region of Earth is a &%GeographicArea.

nodes.label: Atom
nodes.definition: An extremely small unit of matter that retains its identity in Chemical reactions. It consists of an &%AtomicNucleus and &%Electrons surrounding the &%AtomicNucleus.

nodes.label: Atomic Nucleus
nodes.definition: The core of the &%Atom. It is composed of &%Protons and &%Neutrons.

nodes.label: Audio
nodes.definition: A representation or recording of sound.

nodes.label: Automaton
nodes.definition: An abstract machine that changes state while processing input.

nodes.label: Bacterium
nodes.definition: A small, typically one_celled, prokaryotic &%Microorganism.

nodes.label: Battle
nodes.definition: A &%ViolentContest between two or more military units within the context of a war. Note that this does not cover the metaphorical sense of 'battle', which simply means a struggle of some sort. This sense should be represented with the more general concept of &%Contest.

nodes.label: Belief
nodes.definition: A proposition or representation accepted by an agent.

nodes.label: Beverage
nodes.definition: Any food that is ; ingested by &%Drinking. ;Note that this class is disjoint &%Meat and ; &%FruitOrVegetable.

nodes.label: Biological Process
nodes.definition: A &%Process embodied in an &%Organism.

nodes.label: Biologically Active Substance
nodes.definition: A &%Substance that is capable of inducing a change in the structure or functioning of an &%Organism. This &%Class includes &%Substances used in the treatment, diagnosis, prevention or analysis of normal and abnormal body function. This &%Class also includes &%Substances that occur naturally in the body and are administered therapeutically. Finally, &%BiologicallyActiveSubstance includes &%Nutrients, most drugs of abuse, and agents that require special handling because of their toxicity.

nodes.label: Bird
nodes.definition: A &%Vertebrate having a constant body temperature and characterized by the presence of feathers.

nodes.label: Birth
nodes.definition: The &%Process of being born.

nodes.label: Blood
nodes.definition: A fluid present in &%Animals that transports &%Nutrients to and waste products away from various &%BodyParts.

nodes.label: Body Covering
nodes.definition: Any &%BodyPart which is a covering of another &%BodyPart or of an entire &%Organism. This would include the rinds of &%FruitOrVegetables and the skins of &%Animals.

nodes.label: Body Junction
nodes.definition: The place where two &%BodyParts meet or connect.

nodes.label: Body Motion
nodes.definition: Any &%Motion where the &%agent is an &%Organism and the &%patient is a &%BodyPart.

nodes.label: Body Part
nodes.definition: A collection of &%Cells and &%Tissues which are localized to a specific area of an &%Organism and which are not pathological. The instances of this &%Class range from gross structures to small components of complex &%Organs.

nodes.label: Body Substance
nodes.definition: Extracellular material and mixtures of cells and extracellular material that are produced, excreted or accreted by an &%Organism. Included here are &%Substances such as saliva, dental enamel, sweat, hormones, and gastric acid.

nodes.label: Body Vessel
nodes.definition: Any tube-like structure which occurs naturally in an &%Organism and through which a &%BodySubstance can circulate.

nodes.label: Boiling
nodes.definition: The &%Class of &%Processes where a &%Substance is heated and converted from a &%Liquid to a &%Gas.

nodes.label: Bone
nodes.definition: Parts of the body that are made up of &%BoneTissue.

nodes.label: Book
nodes.definition: A &%Document that has pages and is bound.

nodes.label: Building
nodes.definition: The Class of &%StationaryArtifacts which are intended to house &%Humans and their activities.

nodes.label: Canine
nodes.definition: The &%Class of &%Carnivores with completely separable toes, nonretractable claws, and long muzzles.

nodes.label: Capability
nodes.definition: A property representing what an entity can do or undergo.

nodes.label: Carbohydrate
nodes.definition: A compound of living cells and a source of energy for &%Animals. This class includes both simple &%Carbohydrates, i.e. sugars, and complex &%Carbohydrates, i.e. starches.

nodes.label: Carnivore
nodes.definition: The &%DietaryAttribute of flesh-eating &%Organisms. Members with this &%DietaryAttribute typically have four or five claws on each paw. Includes cats, dogs, bears, racoons, and skunks.

nodes.label: Causal relation
nodes.definition: A relation in which one entity contributes to an effect.

nodes.label: Cell
nodes.definition: The fundamental structural and functional unit of living &%Organisms.

nodes.label: Change Of Possession
nodes.definition: The &%Class of &%Processes where ownership of something is transferred from one &%AutonomousAgent to another.

nodes.label: Character
nodes.definition: An element of an alphabet, a set of numerals, etc. Note that a &%Character may or may not be part of a &%Language. &%Character is a subclass of &%SymbolicString, because every instance of &%Character is an alphanumeric sequence consisting of a single element.

nodes.label: Chemical Decomposition
nodes.definition: The &%Class of &%ChemicalProcesses in which a &%CompoundSubstance breaks down into simpler products.

nodes.label: Chemical Process
nodes.definition: A &%ChemicalProcess occurs whenever chemical compounds (&%CompoundSubstances) are formed or decomposed. For example, reactants disappear as chemical change occurs, and products appear as chemical change occurs. In a chemical change a chemical reaction takes place. Catalysts in a &%ChemicalProcess may speed up the reaction, but aren't themselves produced or consumed. Examples: rusting of iron and the decomposition of water, induced by an electric current, to gaseous hydrogen and gaseous oxygen.

nodes.label: Chemical Synthesis
nodes.definition: The &%Class of &%ChemicalProcesses in which a &%CompoundSubstance is formed from simpler reactants.

nodes.label: Circle
nodes.definition: A plane curve whose points are equidistant from a center.

nodes.label: Classification
nodes.definition: A representation that assigns entities to categories.

nodes.label: Classification relation
nodes.definition: A relation that assigns an entity to a kind or category.

nodes.label: Clothing
nodes.definition: &%Artifact made out of fabrics and possibly other materials that are used to cover the bodies of &%Humans.

nodes.label: Club
nodes.definition: An organization formed around shared membership or activity.

nodes.label: Cognitive Agent
nodes.definition: A &%CognitiveAgent is an &%AutonomousAgent that has the ability to reason, deliberate, make plans, and experience emotions. Although &%Human is a subclass of &%CognitiveAgent, there may be instances of &%CognitiveAgent which are not also instances of &%Human. For example, &%Primates, dolphins, whales, and some extraterrestrials (if they exist) might be considered &%CognitiveAgents.

nodes.label: Cold Blooded Vertebrate
nodes.definition: &%Vertebrates whose body temperature is not internally regulated.

nodes.label: Collection
nodes.definition: Collections have &%members like &%Classes, but, unlike &%Classes, they have a position in space-time and &%members can be added and subtracted without thereby changing the identity of the &%Collection. Some examples are toolkits, repeated actions, football teams, and flocks of sheep.

nodes.label: Coloring
nodes.definition: The &%subclass of &%SurfaceChange where a &%ColorAttribute of the &%patient is altered. Note that the change in color may apply to just part of the object.

nodes.label: Communication
nodes.definition: A &%SocialInteraction that involves the transfer of information between two or more &%CognitiveAgents. Note that &%Communication is closely related to, but essentially different from, &%ContentDevelopment. The latter involves the creation or modification of a &%ContentBearingObject, while &%Communication is the transfer of information for the purpose of conveying a message.

nodes.label: Community
nodes.definition: People connected by shared place, identity, activity, or practice.

nodes.label: Complexity class
nodes.definition: A set of computational problems sharing a resource bound.

nodes.label: Compound Substance
nodes.definition: The &%Class of &%Substances that contain two or more elements (&%ElementalSubstances) in definite proportion by weight. The composition of a pure compound will be invariant, regardless of the method of preparation. Compounds are composed of more than one kind of atom (element). The term molecule is often used for the smallest unit of a compound that still retains all of the properties of the compound. Examples: Table salt (sodium chloride, NaCl), sugar (sucrose, C_{12}H_{22}O_{11}), and water (H_2O).

nodes.label: Computable function
nodes.definition: A function for which an effective computation produces each result.

nodes.label: Computational entity
nodes.definition: An entity used to specify, perform, or analyze computation.

nodes.label: Computer Language
nodes.definition: The class of &%Languages designed for and interpreted by a computer.

nodes.label: Condensing
nodes.definition: The &%Class of &%Processes where an &%Object is cooled and converted from a &%Gas to a &%Liquid.

nodes.label: Constructed Language
nodes.definition: An &%ConstructedLanguage is a &%HumanLanguage that did not evolve spontaneously within a language community, but rather had its core grammar and vocabulary invented by one or more language experts, often with an aim to produce a more grammatically regular language than any language that has evolved naturally. This &%Class includes languages like Esperanto that were created to facilitate international communication.

nodes.label: Constructing
nodes.definition: The &%subclass of &%Making in which a &%StationaryArtifact is built.

nodes.label: Content Bearing Object
nodes.definition: Any &%SelfConnectedObject that expresses content. This content may be a &%Proposition, e.g. when the &%ContentBearingObject is a &%Sentence or &%Text, or it may be a representation of an abstract or physical object, as with an &%Icon, a &%Word or a &%Phrase.

nodes.label: Content Development
nodes.definition: A &%subclass of &%IntentionalProcess in which content is modified, its form is altered or it is created anew.

nodes.label: Contest
nodes.definition: A &%SocialInteraction where the &%agent and &%patient are &%CognitiveAgents who are trying to defeat one another. Note that this concept is often applied in a metaphorical sense in natural language, when we speak, e.g., of the struggle of plants for space or sunlight, or of bacteria for food resources in some environment.

nodes.label: Continent
nodes.definition: As defined in the CIA World Fact Book, &%Continent covers seven land masses: &%Africa, &%NorthAmerica, &%SouthAmerica, &%Antarctica, &%Europe, &%Asia, and &%Oceania. Note that &%Australia, counted as a continent in some other systems, is included in &%Oceania in the Fact Book. As a consequence, there is no &%Nation which is also a &%Continent.

nodes.label: Contract
nodes.definition: An agreement recognized as creating enforceable commitments.

nodes.label: Convention
nodes.definition: A practice or meaning maintained by social acceptance.

nodes.label: Cooking
nodes.definition: The &%Making of an &%instance of &%Food. Note that this can cover any preparation of &%Food, e.g. making a salad, cutting up fruit, etc. It does not necessarily involve the application of heat.

nodes.label: Cooling
nodes.definition: Any &%Decreasing &%Process where the &%PhysicalQuantity decreased is a &%TemperatureMeasure.

nodes.label: Cooperation
nodes.definition: The &%subclass of &%SocialInteraction where the participants involved work together for the achievement of a common goal.

nodes.label: Corporation
nodes.definition: A legally recognized organization with a distinct institutional identity.

nodes.label: Corpuscular Object
nodes.definition: A &%SelfConnectedObject whose parts have properties that are not shared by the whole.

nodes.label: Court
nodes.definition: An institution authorized to interpret or apply law.

nodes.label: Creation
nodes.definition: The &%subclass of &%Process in which something is created. Note that the thing created is specified with the &%result &%CaseRole.

nodes.label: Currency
nodes.definition: A socially or institutionally accepted medium of exchange.

nodes.label: Curve
nodes.definition: A one-dimensional geometric entity that varies continuously.

nodes.label: Damaging
nodes.definition: The &%Class of &%Processes where the &%agent brings about a situation where the &%patient no longer functions normally or as intended.

nodes.label: Data
nodes.definition: Recorded content available for interpretation or processing.

nodes.label: Dataset
nodes.definition: A collection of related data items treated as a unit.

nodes.label: Death
nodes.definition: The &%Process of dying.

nodes.label: Decreasing
nodes.definition: Any &%QuantityChange where the &%PhysicalQuantity is decreased.

nodes.label: Definition
nodes.definition: An expression that fixes the meaning or use of a term.

nodes.label: Description
nodes.definition: A representation that conveys characteristics of an entity.

nodes.label: Destruction
nodes.definition: The &%subclass of &%Damagings in which the &%patient (or an essential element of the &%patient) is destroyed. Note that the difference between this concept and its superclass is solely one of extent.

nodes.label: Device
nodes.definition: A &%Device is an &%Artifact whose purpose is to serve as an &%instrument in a specific subclass of &%Process.

nodes.label: Diagnostic Process
nodes.definition: A &%Process that is carried out for the purpose of determining the nature of a &%DiseaseOrSyndrome.

nodes.label: Digesting
nodes.definition: The &%Process by which food that has been ingested is broken down into simpler chemical compounds and absorbed by the &%Organism.

nodes.label: Directing
nodes.definition: Instances of this &%Class urge some further action among the receivers. A &%Directing can be an &%Ordering, a &%Requesting or a &%Questioning.

nodes.label: Disposition
nodes.definition: A property that makes an entity liable to behave in a certain way.

nodes.label: Disseminating
nodes.definition: Any &%Communication that involves a single &%agent and many &%destinations. This covers the release of a published book, broadcasting, a theatrical performance, giving orders to assembled troops, delivering a public lecture, etc.

nodes.label: Document
nodes.definition: A bounded representational work preserved for reading or reference.

nodes.label: Dual Object Process
nodes.definition: Any &%Process that requires two, nonidentical &%patients.

nodes.label: Educational Organization
nodes.definition: A &%EducationalOrganization is an institution of learning. Some examples are public and private K-12 schools, and colleges and universities.

nodes.label: Educational Process
nodes.definition: Any &%Process which is intended to result in &%Learning.

nodes.label: Electron
nodes.definition: &%SubatomicParticles that surround the &%AtomicNucleus. They have a negative charge.

nodes.label: Elemental Substance
nodes.definition: The &%Class of &%PureSubstances that cannot be separated into two or more &%Substances by ordinary chemical (or physical) means. This excludes nuclear reactions. &%ElementalSubstances are composed of only one kind of atom. Examples: Iron (Fe), copper (Cu), and oxygen (O_2). &%ElementalSubstances are the simplest &%PureSubstances.

nodes.label: Ellipse
nodes.definition: A closed plane curve whose distances to two foci have a constant sum.

nodes.label: Engineering Component
nodes.definition: A fundamental concept that applies in many engineering domains. An &%EngineeringComponent is an element of a &%Device that is a physically whole object, such as one might see listed as standard parts in a catalog. The main difference betweeen &%EngineeringComponents and arbitrary globs of matter is that &%EngineeringComponents are object-like in a modeling sense. Thus, an &%EngineeringComponent is not an arbtrary subregion, but a part of a system with a stable identity.

nodes.label: Engineering Connection
nodes.definition: An &%EngineeringConnection is an &%EngineeringComponent that represents a connection relationship between two other &%EngineeringComponents. It is a reification of the &%Predicate &%connectedEngineeringComponents. That means that whenever this &%Predicate holds between two &%EngineeringComponents, there exists an &%EngineeringConnection. The practical reason for reifying a relationship is to be able to attach other information about it. For example, one might want to say that a particular connection is associated with some shared parameters, or that it is of a particular type. &%EngineeringConnections are &%EngineeringComponents and can therefore be an &%engineeringSubcomponent of other &%EngineeringComponents. However, to provide for modular regularity in component systems, &%EngineeringConnections cannot be connected. For each pair of &%EngineeringComponents related by &%connectedEngineeringComponents, there exists at least one &%EngineeringConnection. However, that object may not be unique, and the same &%EngineeringConnection may be associated with several pairs of &%EngineeringComponents.

nodes.label: Entity
nodes.definition: An entity considered as a bearer of properties or participant in relations.

nodes.label: Enzyme
nodes.definition: A complex &%Protein that is produced by living cells and which catalyzes specific biochemical reactions. There are six main types of enzymes: oxidoreductases, transferases, hydrolases, lyases, isomerases, and ligases.

nodes.label: Epistemic relation
nodes.definition: A relation concerning knowledge, belief, evidence, or justification.

nodes.label: Equivalence relation
nodes.definition: A relation grouping entities as interchangeable under specified criteria.

nodes.label: Ethnic Group
nodes.definition: A &%GroupOfPeople whose &%members originate from the same &%GeographicArea or share the same &%Language and/or cultural practices.

nodes.label: Event
nodes.definition: A bounded occurrence recognized as socially or otherwise significant.

nodes.label: Explanatory relation
nodes.definition: A relation in which one entity accounts for another.

nodes.label: Fabric
nodes.definition: &%Artifacts that are created by weaving together natural or synthetic fibers or by treating the skins of certain sorts of &%Animals. Note that this &%Class includes articles that are created by stitching together various types of fabrics, e.g. bedspreads. On the other hand, &%Clothing is not a &%subclass of &%Fabric, because many clothing items contain elements that are not fabrics.

nodes.label: Fact
nodes.definition: A proposition treated as supported or established.

nodes.label: Family Group
nodes.definition: A &%GroupOfPeople whose &%members bear &%familyRelations to one another.

nodes.label: Fat Tissue
nodes.definition: Nonrigid &%Tissue that is composed largely of fat cells.

nodes.label: Feline
nodes.definition: The &%Class of &%Carnivores with completely separable toes, slim bodies, and rounded heads. All felines other than the cheetah have retractable claws.

nodes.label: Fern
nodes.definition: A &%NonFloweringPlant that contains vascular tissue. This class includes true ferns, as well as horsetails, club mosses, and whisk ferns.

nodes.label: Financial Transaction
nodes.definition: A &%Transaction where an instance of &%FinancialInstrument is the subject of the action, and often is exchanged for something else.

nodes.label: Fish
nodes.definition: A cold-blooded aquatic &%Vertebrate characterized by fins and breathing by gills. Included here are &%Fish having either a bony skeleton, such as a perch, or a cartilaginous skeleton, such as a shark. Also included are those &%Fish lacking a jaw, such as a lamprey or hagfish.

nodes.label: Flowering Plant
nodes.definition: A &%Plant that produces seeds and flowers. This class includes trees, shrubs, herbs, and flowers.

nodes.label: Food
nodes.definition: Food that is fit for &%Human.

nodes.label: Formal expression
nodes.definition: A well-formed symbolic construction in a formal language.

nodes.label: Formal language
nodes.definition: A set of strings formed according to specified symbols and rules.

nodes.label: Freezing
nodes.definition: The &%Class of &%Processes where an &%Object is cooled and converted from a &%Liquid to a &%Solid.

nodes.label: Fresh Water Area
nodes.definition: A &%WaterArea whose &%Water is not saline, e.g. most rivers and lakes.

nodes.label: Fruit
nodes.definition: &%Fruits comes from the flowering &part of a &%FloweringPlant and contain &%Seeds. [Wikipedia]

nodes.label: Function
nodes.definition: A rule or entity that assigns each allowed input a result.

nodes.label: Fungus
nodes.definition: A eukaryotic &%Organism characterized by the absence of chlorophyll and the presence of rigid cell walls. Included here are both slime molds and true fungi such as yeasts, molds, mildews, and mushrooms.

nodes.label: Game
nodes.definition: A &%Contest whose purpose is the enjoyment/stimulation of the participants or spectators of the &%Game.

nodes.label: Geographic Area
nodes.definition: A geographic location, generally having definite boundaries. Note that this differs from its immediate superclass &%Region in that a &%GeographicArea is a three-dimensional &%Region of the earth. Accordingly, all astronomical objects other than earth and all one-dimensional and two-dimensional &%Regions are not classed under &%GeographicArea.

nodes.label: Geometric entity
nodes.definition: An entity characterized by spatial form, location, or extension.

nodes.label: Geopolitical Area
nodes.definition: Any &%GeographicArea which is associated with some sort of political structure. This class includes &%LandArea, &%Cities, districts of cities, counties, etc. Note that the identity of a &%GeopoliticalArea may remain constant after a change in borders.

nodes.label: Getting
nodes.definition: The &%subclass of &%ChangeOfPossession where the &%agent gets something. Note that the source from which something is obtained is specified with the &%origin &%CaseRole.

nodes.label: Giving
nodes.definition: The &%subclass of &%ChangeOfPossession where the &%agent gives the &%destination something.

nodes.label: Gland
nodes.definition: An &%Organ that removes &%Substances from the &%Blood,alters them in some way, and then releases them.

nodes.label: Goal
nodes.definition: A desired or intended state treated as an end.

nodes.label: Government
nodes.definition: The ruling body of a &%GeopoliticalArea.

nodes.label: Graph
nodes.definition: An entity consisting of vertices connected by edges.

nodes.label: Group
nodes.definition: A &%CollectionOfObjects of &%Agents, e.g. a flock of sheep, a herd of goats, or the local Boy Scout troop.

nodes.label: Growth
nodes.definition: The &%Process of biological development in which an &%Organism or part of an &%Organism changes its form or its size.

nodes.label: Guiding
nodes.definition: Any &%IntentionalProcess where the &%agent tries to direct the behavior of another &%Object, whether an &%AutonomousAgent or not.

nodes.label: Heating
nodes.definition: Any &%Increasing &%Process where the &%PhysicalQuantity increased is a &%TemperatureMeasure.

nodes.label: Hominid
nodes.definition: Includes &%Humans and relatively recent ancestors of &%Humans.

nodes.label: Hoofed Mammal
nodes.definition: The &%Class of quadruped &%Mammals with hooves. Includes horses, cows, sheep, pigs, antelope, etc.

nodes.label: Hormone
nodes.definition: In &%Animals, a chemical secreted by an endocrine gland whose products are released into the circulating fluid. &%Plant hormones or synthetic hormones which are used only to alter or control various physiologic processes, e.g., reproductive control agents, are assigned to the &%Class &%BiologicallyActiveSubstance. &%Hormones act as chemical messengers and regulate various physiologic processes such as growth, reproduction, metabolism, etc. They usually fall into two broad categories, viz. steroid hormones and peptide hormones.

nodes.label: Human
nodes.definition: Modern man, the only remaining species of the Homo genus.

nodes.label: Human Language
nodes.definition: The &%subclass of &%Languages used by &%Humans.

nodes.label: Hyperbola
nodes.definition: A curve whose points have a constant difference of distances to two foci.

nodes.label: Icon
nodes.definition: This is the subclass of &%ContentBearingPhysical which are not part of a &%Language and which have some sort of similarity with the &%Objects that they represent. This &%Class would include symbolic roadway signs, representational art works, photographs, etc.

nodes.label: Identity relation
nodes.definition: A relation stating that entities are the same entity.

nodes.label: Image
nodes.definition: A representation that conveys visual form or appearance.

nodes.label: Impelling
nodes.definition: The &%subclass of &%Transfer where the &%patient travels through space by means of a sudden, forceful event. Some examples would be shooting, throwing, tossing, etc.

nodes.label: Increasing
nodes.definition: Any &%QuantityChange where the &%PhysicalQuantity is increased.

nodes.label: Informational entity
nodes.definition: An entity whose identity depends on content, evidence, or information.

nodes.label: Ingesting
nodes.definition: The &%Process by which food or &%Medicine is taken into an &%Animal.

nodes.label: Injuring
nodes.definition: The process of creating a traumatic wound or injury. Since &%Injuring is not possible without some biologic function of the organism being injured, it is a subclass of &%BiologicalProcess.

nodes.label: Institution
nodes.definition: A durable social arrangement organized around recognized practices or rules.

nodes.label: Institutional entity
nodes.definition: A durable rule-governed social entity with recognized functions or authority.

nodes.label: Institutional relation
nodes.definition: A relation defined by an institution, rule, or office.

nodes.label: Intentional Process
nodes.definition: A &%Process that has a specific purpose for the &%AutonomousAgent who performs it.

nodes.label: Intentional Psychological Process
nodes.definition: An &%IntentionalProcess is a process that can be realized entirely within the mind or brain of an &%Organism. Thus,for example, &%Reasoning is a subclass of &%IntentionalPsychologicalProcess, because one can reason simply by exercising one's mind/brain. On the other hand, &%RecreationOrExercise is not a subclass of &%IntentionalPsychologicalProcess, because many instances of &%RecreationOrExercise necessarily have &%subProcesses of &%BodyMotion.

nodes.label: Internal Change
nodes.definition: &%Processes which involve altering an internal property of an &%Object, e.g. the shape of the &%Object, its coloring, its structure, etc. &%Processes that are not instances of this class include changes that only affect the relationship to other objects, e.g. changes in spatial or temporal location.

nodes.label: Invertebrate
nodes.definition: An &%Animal which has no spinal column.

nodes.label: Investigating
nodes.definition: The class of &%IntentionalPsychologicalProcesses where the &%agent attempts to obtain information (i.e. a &%Proposition denoted by a &%Formula).

nodes.label: Island
nodes.definition: A &%LandArea that is completely surrounded by a &%WaterArea.

nodes.label: Joining An Organization
nodes.definition: The &%OrganizationalProcess of becoming a &%member of an &%Organization.

nodes.label: Keeping
nodes.definition: The &%Class of &%Processes where the &%agent keeps something in a particular location for an extended period of time.

nodes.label: Knowledge
nodes.definition: Information regarded as understood, justified, or usable.

nodes.label: Label
nodes.definition: A name or mark attached to an entity for identification or classification.

nodes.label: Land Area
nodes.definition: An area which is predominantly solid ground, e.g. a &%Nation, a mountain, a desert, etc. Note that a &%LandArea may contain some relatively small &%WaterAreas. For example, Australia is a &%LandArea even though it contains various rivers and lakes.

nodes.label: Language
nodes.definition: A system of signs for expressing thought. The system can be either natural or artificial, i.e. something that emerges gradually as a cultural artifact or something that is intentionally created by a person or group of people.

nodes.label: Law
nodes.definition: A rule recognized and enforced by an authority or legal system.

nodes.label: Leaving An Organization
nodes.definition: The &%OrganizationalProcess of leaving an &%Organization, whether voluntarily or involuntarily.

nodes.label: Legal Action
nodes.definition: Any &%Process where a &%CognitiveAgent seeks to obtain something through a court of law.

nodes.label: License
nodes.definition: An authorization granted under specified conditions.

nodes.label: Linguistic Communication
nodes.definition: A &%Communication that involves the transfer of information via a &%LinguisticExpression.

nodes.label: Linguistic Expression
nodes.definition: This is the subclass of &%ContentBearingPhysical which are language-related. Note that this &%Class encompasses both &%Language and the the elements of &%Languages, e.g. &%Words.

nodes.label: Logical entity
nodes.definition: An entity used to express or evaluate logical form.

nodes.label: Logical property
nodes.definition: A property defined by logical form or consequence.

nodes.label: Logical relation
nodes.definition: A relation defined by logical form or consequence.

nodes.label: Machine
nodes.definition: &%Machines are &%Devices that that have a well-defined &%resource and &%result and that automatically convert the &%resource into the &%result.

nodes.label: Maintaining
nodes.definition: The &%Class of &%Processes where the &%agent cares for or maintains the &%Object.

nodes.label: Making
nodes.definition: The &%subclass of &%Creation in which an individual &%Artifact or a type of &%Artifact is made.

nodes.label: Mammal
nodes.definition: A &%Vertebrate having a constant body temperature and characterized by the presence of hair, mammary glands, and sweat glands.

nodes.label: Managing
nodes.definition: &%OrganizationalProcesses that involve overseeing the activities of others. Note the key differences between &%RegulatoryProcess and its sibling &%Managing. The latter implies a long-term relationship between the manager and the managed, while the former implies a normative standard to which the activities of the regulated are referred.

nodes.label: Maneuver
nodes.definition: An intentional move or play within a &%Contest. In many cases, a &%Maneuver is a realization of part of a strategy for winning the &%Contest, but it also may be just an arbitrary or semi-arbitrary division of the overarching &%Contest, e.g. innings in a baseball game.

nodes.label: Manufacture
nodes.definition: The &%Making of &%Artifacts on a mass scale.

nodes.label: Market
nodes.definition: An institution or arrangement for exchange among participants.

nodes.label: Marsupial
nodes.definition: The &%Class of &%Mammals which have a pouch for their young.

nodes.label: Mathematical entity
nodes.definition: An abstract entity used in mathematical description, reasoning, or construction.

nodes.label: Mathematical model
nodes.definition: A mathematical representation of a target system or situation.

nodes.label: Mathematical property
nodes.definition: A characteristic defined or established mathematically.

nodes.label: Mathematical relation
nodes.definition: A relation defined between mathematical entities.

nodes.label: Measurement
nodes.definition: A reported comparison of a quantity with a scale or standard.

nodes.label: Meat
nodes.definition: Any food which was originally part of an &%Animal and is not ingested by drinking, including eggs and animal blood that is eaten as food. Note that this class covers both raw meat and meat that has been prepared in some way, e.g. by cooking. Note too that preparations involving &%Meat and &%FruitOrVegetable are classed directly under &%Food.

nodes.label: Meeting
nodes.definition: The coming together of two or more &%CognitiveAgents for the purpose of &%Communication. This covers informal meetings, e.g. visits with family members, and formal meetings, e.g. a board of directors meeting.

nodes.label: Melting
nodes.definition: The &%Class of &%Processes where an &%Object is heated and converted from a &%Solid to a &%Liquid.

nodes.label: Message
nodes.definition: Information intended to be conveyed from a source to a recipient.

nodes.label: Metal
nodes.definition: A &%Metal is an &%ElementalSubstance that conducts heat and electricity, is shiny and reflects many colors of light, and can be hammered into sheets or drawn into wire. About 80% of the known chemical elements (&%ElementalSubstances) are metals.

nodes.label: Military Process
nodes.definition: &%Process that is carried out by a military organization. Note that this class covers &%Processes, e.g. military operations, that are the result of careful planning, as well as those which are unscripted.

nodes.label: Mineral
nodes.definition: Any of various naturally occurring homogeneous substances (such as stone, coal, salt, sulfur, sand, petroleum), or synthetic substances having the chemical composition and crystalline form and properties of a naturally occurring mineral.

nodes.label: Mixture
nodes.definition: A &%Mixture is two or more &%PureSubstances, combined in varying proportions - each retaining its own specific properties. The components of a &%Mixture can be separated by physical means, i.e. without the making and breaking of chemical bonds. Examples: Air, table salt thoroughly dissolved in water, milk, wood, and concrete.

nodes.label: Modal property
nodes.definition: A property concerning possibility, necessity, or contingency.

nodes.label: Model
nodes.definition: A representation used to describe, explain, predict, or guide.

nodes.label: Molecule
nodes.definition: A molecule is the smallest unit of matter of a &%CompoundSubstance that retains all the physical and chemical properties of that substance, e.g., Ne, H2, H2O. A molecule is two or more &%Atoms linked by a chemical bond.

nodes.label: Monkey
nodes.definition: Various &%Primates with relatively long tails.

nodes.label: Morpheme
nodes.definition: Part of a &%Word which cannot be subdivided and which expresses a meaning.

nodes.label: Moss
nodes.definition: A &%NonFloweringPlant without true roots and little if any vascular tissue.

nodes.label: Motion
nodes.definition: Any &%Process of movement.

nodes.label: Motion Picture
nodes.definition: A &%ContentBearingObject which depicts motion (and which may have an audio or text component as well). This &%Class covers films, videos, etc.

nodes.label: Muscle
nodes.definition: A &%Muscle is a kind of &%BodyPart consisting of contractile tissue that allows for movement of the &%AnatomicalStructure through the contraction and relaxation of fibers.

nodes.label: Musical Instrument
nodes.definition: A &%Device which is manipulated by a &%Human and whose purpose is &%MakingMusic.

nodes.label: Name
nodes.definition: A symbol or expression used to identify an entity.

nodes.label: Natural Language
nodes.definition: The &%subclass of &%HumanLanguages which are not designed and which evolve from generation to generation. This &%Class includes all of the national languages, e.g. English, Spanish, Japanese, etc. Note that this class includes dialects of natural languages.

nodes.label: Neutron
nodes.definition: Components of the &%AtomicNucleus. They have no charge.

nodes.label: Non Flowering Plant
nodes.definition: A &%Plant that reproduces with spores and does not produce flowers.

nodes.label: Norm
nodes.definition: A rule or standard specifying expected conduct or form.

nodes.label: Notation
nodes.definition: A conventional system of symbols used to express entities or relations.

nodes.label: Noun
nodes.definition: One of the parts of speech. The &%Class of &%Words that conventionally denote &%Objects.

nodes.label: Noun Phrase
nodes.definition: A &%Phrase that has the same function as a &%Noun.

nodes.label: Number
nodes.definition: An entity that specifies a count, magnitude, or position.

nodes.label: Nutrient
nodes.definition: A &%BiologicallyActiveSubstance required by an &%Organism. It is generally ingested as food, and it is of primary interest because of its role in the biologic functioning of the &%Organism.

nodes.label: Object
nodes.definition: A bounded entity considered apart from its properties and relations.

nodes.label: Obligation
nodes.definition: A requirement binding an agent to an action or state.

nodes.label: Observation
nodes.definition: Information acquired by attending to an entity or event.

nodes.label: Office
nodes.definition: An institutional position or the authority associated with it.

nodes.label: Ontology
nodes.definition: A structured account of kinds and relations in a domain.

nodes.label: Organ
nodes.definition: A somewhat independent &%BodyPart that performs a specialized function. Note that this functional definition covers bodily systems, e.g. the digestive system or the central nervous system.

nodes.label: Organ Or Tissue Process
nodes.definition: A &%PhysiologicProcess of a particular &%Organ or &%Tissue.

nodes.label: Organic Object
nodes.definition: This class encompasses &%Organisms, &%CorpuscularObjects that are parts of &%Organisms, i.e. &%BodyParts, and &%CorpuscularObjects that are nonintentionally produced by &%Organisms, e.g. &%ReproductiveBodies.

nodes.label: Organism
nodes.definition: Generally, a living individual, including all &%Plants and &%Animals.

nodes.label: Organism Process
nodes.definition: A physiologic function of the &%Organism as a whole, of multiple organ systems or of multiple &%Organs or &%Tissues.

nodes.label: Organization
nodes.definition: An &%Organization is a corporate or similar institution. The &%members of an &%Organization typically have a common purpose or function. Note that this class also covers divisions, departments, etc. of organizations. For example, both the Shell Oil Corporation and the accounting department at Shell would both be instances of &%Organization. Note too that the existence of an &%Organization is dependent on the existence of at least one &%member (since &%Organization is a subclass of &%CollectionOfObjects). Accordingly, in cases of purely legal organizations, a fictitious &%member should be assumed.

nodes.label: Organizational Process
nodes.definition: An &%IntentionalProcess that involves an &%Organization.

nodes.label: Parabola
nodes.definition: A plane curve whose points are equidistant from a focus and a directrix.

nodes.label: Part-whole relation
nodes.definition: A relation between a whole and one of its parts.

nodes.label: Participation relation
nodes.definition: A relation connecting an entity with an event or process it takes part in.

nodes.label: Patent
nodes.definition: A &%Certificate that expresses the content of an invention that has been accorded legal protection by a governemental entity.

nodes.label: Pathologic Process
nodes.definition: A disordered process, activity, or state of the &%Organism as a whole, of a body system or systems, or of multiple &%Organs or &%Tissues. Included here are normal responses to a negative stimulus as well as patholologic conditions or states that are less specific than a disease. Pathologic functions frequently have systemic effects.

nodes.label: Perception
nodes.definition: Sensing some aspect of the material world. Note that the &%agent of this sensing is assumed to be an &%Animal.

nodes.label: Perceptual relation
nodes.definition: A relation between a perceiver and what is perceived.

nodes.label: Periodical
nodes.definition: A &%Series whose elements are published separately and on a periodic basis.

nodes.label: Person
nodes.definition: An individual human being considered as a social participant.

nodes.label: Phrase
nodes.definition: A set of &%Words in a &%Language which form a unit, i.e. express a meaning in the &%Language.

nodes.label: Physical object
nodes.definition: Corresponds roughly to the class of ordinary objects. Examples include normal physical objects, geographical regions, and locations of &%Processes, the complement of &%Objects in the &%Physical class. In a 4D ontology, an &%Object is something whose spatiotemporal extent is thought of as dividing into spatial parts roughly parallel to the time-axis.

nodes.label: Physical system model
nodes.definition: A mathematical entity representing a physical system.

nodes.label: Physiologic Process
nodes.definition: A normal process of an &%Organism or part of an &%Organism.

nodes.label: Plant
nodes.definition: An &%Organism having cellulose cell walls, growing by synthesis of &%Substances, generally distinguished by the presence of chlorophyll, and lacking the power of locomotion.

nodes.label: Poking
nodes.definition: The &%Class of &%Processes where the &%agent pierces the surface of the &%Object with an &%instrument.

nodes.label: Policy
nodes.definition: A rule or principle adopted to guide decisions or conduct.

nodes.label: Political Organization
nodes.definition: An &%Organization that is attempting to bring about some sort of political change.

nodes.label: Political Process
nodes.definition: An &%OrganizationalProcess carried out by, for or against officially constituted governments. Some examples would be voting on proposed legislation, electing a government representative, or even overthrowing a government in a revolution.

nodes.label: Practice
nodes.definition: A recurring activity or method maintained by participants.

nodes.label: Preference
nodes.definition: A disposition to favor one option or state over another.

nodes.label: Prepositional Phrase
nodes.definition: A &%Phrase that begins with a preposition and that functions as an &%Adjective or an &%Adverb.

nodes.label: Primate
nodes.definition: The &%Class of &%Mammals which are &%Primates.

nodes.label: Probability entity
nodes.definition: An entity used to represent chance, uncertainty, or distribution.

nodes.label: Process
nodes.definition: The class of things that happen and have temporal parts or stages. Examples include extended events like a football match or a race, actions like &%Pursuing and &%Reading, and biological processes. The formal definition is: anything that occurs in time but is not an &%Object. Note that a &%Process may have participants 'inside' it which are &%Objects, such as the players in a football match. In a 4D ontology, a &%Process is something whose spatiotemporal extent is thought of as dividing into temporal stages roughly perpendicular to the time-axis.

nodes.label: Product
nodes.definition: An &%Artifact that is produced by &%Manufacture.

nodes.label: Proof
nodes.definition: A finite argument that establishes a proposition from accepted premises.

nodes.label: Property
nodes.definition: A repeatable characteristic, capability, disposition, or value attributable to an entity.

nodes.label: Proposition
nodes.definition: An entity that can be asserted and evaluated as true or false.

nodes.label: Protein
nodes.definition: A &%Nutrient made up of amino acids joined by peptide bonds.

nodes.label: Proton
nodes.definition: Components of the &%AtomicNucleus. They have a positive charge.

nodes.label: Provenance relation
nodes.definition: A relation recording an entity's source, derivation, or history.

nodes.label: Psychological Process
nodes.definition: A &%BiologicalProcess which takes place in the mind or brain of an &%Organism and which may be manifested in the behavior of the &%Organism.

nodes.label: Publication
nodes.definition: The &%Manufacture of &%Texts. Note that there is no implication that the &%Texts are distributed. Such distribution, when it occurs, is an instance of &%Dissemination.

nodes.label: Pure Substance
nodes.definition: The &%Class of &%Substances with constant composition. A &%PureSubstance can be either an element (&%ElementalSubstance) or a compound of elements (&%CompoundSubstance). Examples: Table salt (sodium chloride, NaCl), sugar (sucrose, C_{12}H_{22}O_{11}), water (H_2O), iron (Fe), copper (Cu), and oxygen (O_2).

nodes.label: Purpose
nodes.definition: An intended end that guides an entity or activity.

nodes.label: Putting
nodes.definition: The &%Class of &%Processes where something is put in a location. Note that the location is specified with the &%CaseRole &%destination.

nodes.label: Quality
nodes.definition: A characteristic describing how an entity is.

nodes.label: Quality value
nodes.definition: A value that specifies a quality on a scale or comparison.

nodes.label: Quantity
nodes.definition: A property specifying how many, how much, or to what extent.

nodes.label: Quantity Change
nodes.definition: Any &%InternalChange where a &%PhysicalQuantity associated with the &%patient is altered.

nodes.label: Radiating
nodes.definition: Processes in which some form of electromagnetic radiation, e.g. radio waves, light waves, electrical energy, etc., is given off or absorbed by something else.

nodes.label: Radiating Light
nodes.definition: The &%subclass of &%Radiating in which light is given off or absorbed. Some examples include blinking, flashing, and glittering.

nodes.label: Radiating Sound
nodes.definition: The &%subclass of &%Radiating in which sound waves are given off or absorbed. Some examples include creaking, roaring, and whistling.

nodes.label: Realized entity
nodes.definition: An entity with a physical embodiment or location in space-time.

nodes.label: Record
nodes.definition: A bounded account of data retained for reference.

nodes.label: Recreation Or Exercise
nodes.definition: A &%Process that is carried out for the purpose of recreation or exercise. Since &%RecreationOrExercise is a subclass of &%IntentionalProcess, the intent of a process determines whether or not it is an instance of the class. Hence, if John and Bill watch the same program on television, and John watches it to relax while Bill watches it solely to satisfy an educational requirement, then John's watching the movie is an instance of &%RecreationOrExercise, while Bill's is not (both cases of watching the television program would however be in the class of &%Seeing, since being an instance of this latter class is not determined by intention).

nodes.label: Recursive function
nodes.definition: A function defined from initial functions by recursion and composition.

nodes.label: Region
nodes.definition: A topographic location. &%Regions encompass surfaces of &%Objects, imaginary places, and &%GeographicAreas. Note that a &%Region is the only kind of &%Object which can be located at itself. Note too that &%Region is not a subclass of &%SelfConnectedObject, because some &%Regions, e.g. archipelagos, have &%parts which are not &%connected with one another.

nodes.label: Regulatory Process
nodes.definition: An &%Guiding whose aim is the enforcement of rules or regulations. Note the key differences between &%RegulatoryProcess and the related concept &%Managing. The latter implies a long-term relationship between a single manager and limited number of agents who are managed, while the former implies a normative standard to which the activities of the regulated are referred.

nodes.label: Relation
nodes.definition: A way in which two or more entities are connected, compared, or ordered.

nodes.label: Relationship
nodes.definition: A socially recognized connection between participants.

nodes.label: Religious Organization
nodes.definition: An &%Organization whose members share a set of religious beliefs.

nodes.label: Religious Process
nodes.definition: An &%OrganizationalProcess that is carried out within or by a &%ReligiousOrganization.

nodes.label: Remembering
nodes.definition: The &%Class of &%PsychologicalProcesses which involve the recollection of prior experiences and/or of knowledge which was previously acquired.

nodes.label: Removing
nodes.definition: The &%Class of &%Processes where something is taken away from a location. Note that the thing removed and the location are specified with the &%CaseRoles &%patient and &%origin, respectively.

nodes.label: Repairing
nodes.definition: The &%Class of &%Processes where the &%agent makes a modification or series of modifications to an &%Object that is not functioning as intended so that it works properly.

nodes.label: Replication
nodes.definition: The &%Process of biological reproduction. This can be either a sexual or an asexual process.

nodes.label: Representational entity
nodes.definition: An entity that encodes, expresses, preserves, or transmits content.

nodes.label: Representational relation
nodes.definition: A relation between content and what represents, encodes, or denotes it.

nodes.label: Reproductive Body
nodes.definition: Reproductive structure of &%Organisms. Consists of an &%Embryonic &%Object and a nutritive/protective envelope. Note that this class includes seeds, spores, and &%FruitOrVegetables, as well as the eggs produced by &%Animals.

nodes.label: Reptile
nodes.definition: A &%ColdBloodedVertebrate having an external covering of scales or horny plates. &%Reptiles breathe by means of &%Lungs and generally lay eggs.

nodes.label: Rodent
nodes.definition: The &%Class of &%Mammals with one or two pairs of incisors for gnawing. Includes rats, mice, guinea pigs, and rabbits.

nodes.label: Role
nodes.definition: A socially recognized position with associated expectations.

nodes.label: Room
nodes.definition: A &%properPart of a &%Building which is separated from the exterior of the &%Building and/or other &%Rooms of the &%Building by walls. Some &%Rooms may have a specific purpose, e.g. sleeping, bathing, cooking, entertainment, etc.

nodes.label: Salt Water Area
nodes.definition: A &%WaterArea whose &%Water is saline, e.g. oceans and seas.

nodes.label: Schema
nodes.definition: A formal plan for the organization of information.

nodes.label: School
nodes.definition: An institution organized for teaching, learning, or scholarly activity.

nodes.label: Searching
nodes.definition: An &%IntentionalProcess which has the purpose for a &%CognitiveAgent to learn the location of a &%Physical.

nodes.label: Self Connected Object
nodes.definition: A &%SelfConnectedObject is any &%Object that does not consist of two or more disconnected parts.

nodes.label: Sentient Agent
nodes.definition: A &%SentientAgent is an &%AutonomousAgent that is capable of &%Perception and experiences some level of consciousness (see &%ConsciousnessAttribute). If the &%AutonomousAgent is able to reason at a comparatively high level (evinced by the ability to learn, plan, and feel emotions), then it is also an instance of &%CognitiveAgent. A &%DomesticAnimal is a &%SentientAgent, but may or may not be a &%CognitiveAgent, depending on the type of &%Animal.

nodes.label: Series
nodes.definition: A &%Text consisting of multiple self-contained units. Some examples are an encyclopedia containing a couple dozen volumes, a television series made up of many episodes, a film serial, etc.

nodes.label: Set
nodes.definition: A collection treated as one abstract entity.

nodes.label: Set-theoretic relation
nodes.definition: A relation involving sets, membership, inclusion, or ordering.

nodes.label: Shape Change
nodes.definition: The &%Process of changing the shape of an &%Object.

nodes.label: Signal
nodes.definition: A perceivable variation that conveys or can convey information.

nodes.label: Social entity
nodes.definition: An entity whose persistence depends on participants, recognition, or shared practice.

nodes.label: Social Interaction
nodes.definition: The &%subclass of &%IntentionalProcess that involves interactions between &%CognitiveAgents.

nodes.label: Social relation
nodes.definition: A relation constituted by social interaction or recognition.

nodes.label: Software
nodes.definition: A program or related information used to control computation.

nodes.label: Solution
nodes.definition: A liquid mixture. The most abundant component in a solution is called the solvent. Other components are called solutes. A solution, though homogeneous, may nonetheless have variable composition. Any amount of salt, up to a maximum limit, can be dissolved in a given amount of water.

nodes.label: Spatial relation
nodes.definition: A relation concerning location, distance, direction, or containment.

nodes.label: Sport
nodes.definition: A &%Game which requires some degree of physical exercion from the participants of the game.

nodes.label: State Change
nodes.definition: Any &%Process where the &%PhysicalState of &%part of the &%patient of the &%Process changes.

nodes.label: Static Water Area
nodes.definition: A &%WaterArea in which water does not flow constantly or in the same direction, e.g. most lakes and ponds.

nodes.label: Stationary Artifact
nodes.definition: A &%StationaryArtifact is an &%Artifact that has a fixed spatial location. Most instances of this &%Class are architectural works, e.g. the Eiffel Tower, the Great Pyramids, office towers, single_family houses, etc.

nodes.label: Status
nodes.definition: A socially recognized standing or condition.

nodes.label: Stream Water Area
nodes.definition: A relatively narrow ; &%WaterArea where the ;water flows constantly and in the same ; direction, e.g. a river, a stream, ;etc.

nodes.label: Subatomic Particle
nodes.definition: The class of &%ElementalSubstances that are smaller than &%Atoms and compose &%Atoms.

nodes.label: Substance
nodes.definition: An &%Object in which every part is similar to every other in every relevant respect. More precisely, something is a &%Substance when it has only arbitrary pieces as parts - any parts have properties which are similar to those of the whole. Note that a &%Substance may nonetheless have physical properties that vary. For example, the temperature, chemical constitution, density, etc. may change from one part to another. An example would be a body of water.

nodes.label: Summary
nodes.definition: A short &%Text that is a summary of another, longer &%Text.

nodes.label: Surface Change
nodes.definition: &%Processes which involve altering the properties that apply to the surface of an &%Object.

nodes.label: Surgery
nodes.definition: Any &%TherapeuticProcess that involves making an incision in the &%Animal that is the &%patient of the &%TherapeuticProcess.

nodes.label: Symbol
nodes.definition: An entity used to stand for or evoke another entity or meaning.

nodes.label: Symbolic String
nodes.definition: The &%Class of alphanumeric sequences.

nodes.label: Tactile Perception
nodes.definition: The &%subclass of &%Perception in which the sensing is done by &%Touching. Note that &%Touching need not involve &%TactilePerception. For example, a person who has lost all sensation in both of his legs would have no &%TactilePerception of anything his legs were &%Touching.

nodes.label: Temporal relation
nodes.definition: A relation concerning time, sequence, or duration.

nodes.label: Text
nodes.definition: A &%LinguisticExpression or set of &%LinguisticExpressions that perform a specific function related to &%Communication, e.g. express a discourse about a particular topic, and that are inscribed in a &%CorpuscularObject by &%Humans.

nodes.label: Theorem
nodes.definition: A proposition established by an accepted proof.

nodes.label: Tissue
nodes.definition: An aggregation of similarly specialized &%Cells and the associated intercellular substance. &%Tissues are relatively non-localized in comparison to &%BodyParts, &%Organs or &%Organ components. The main features of &%Tissues are self-connectivity (see &%SelfConnectedObject) and being a homogeneous mass (all parts in the same granularity are instances of &%Tissue as well).

nodes.label: Topological entity
nodes.definition: An entity defined by continuity, neighborhood, or connectedness.

nodes.label: Touching
nodes.definition: Any &%Transfer where two &%Objects are brought into immediate physical contact with one another.

nodes.label: Toxic Organism
nodes.definition: The &%Class of &%Organisms which are poisonous to other &%Organisms.

nodes.label: Transaction
nodes.definition: The &%subclass of &%ChangeOfPossession where something is exchanged for something else.

nodes.label: Transfer
nodes.definition: Any &%instance of &%Translocation where the &%agent and the &%patient are not the same thing.

nodes.label: Transformation relation
nodes.definition: A relation connecting an entity to a result of changing it.

nodes.label: Transportation
nodes.definition: &%Motion from one point to another by means of a &%TransportationDevice.

nodes.label: Transportation Device
nodes.definition: A &%TransportationDevice is a &%Device which serves as the &%instrument in a &%Transportation &%Process which carries the &%patient of the &%Process from one point to another.

nodes.label: Unilateral Getting
nodes.definition: Any instance of &%Getting that is not part of a &%Transaction. In other words, any instance of &%Getting where nothing is given in return. Some examples of &%UnilateralGetting are: appropriating, commandeering, stealing, etc.

nodes.label: Unilateral Giving
nodes.definition: Any instance of &%Giving that is not part of a &%Transaction. In other words, any instance of &%Giving where nothing is received in return. Some examples of &%UnilateralGiving are: honorary awards, gifts, and financial grants.

nodes.label: Vegetable
nodes.definition: &%Vegetable is a subclass of &%FruitOrVegetable.

nodes.label: Verb
nodes.definition: One of the parts of speech. The &%Class of &%Words that conventionally denote &%Processes.

nodes.label: Verb Phrase
nodes.definition: A &%Phrase that has the same function as a &%Verb.

nodes.label: Vertebrate
nodes.definition: An &%Animal which has a spinal column.

nodes.label: Video
nodes.definition: A representation or recording of moving images, usually with sound.

nodes.label: Violent Contest
nodes.definition: A &%Contest where one participant attempts to physically injure another participant.

nodes.label: Virus
nodes.definition: An &%Organism consisting of a core of a single nucleic acid enclosed in a protective coat of protein. A virus may replicate only inside a host living cell. A virus exhibits some but not all of the usual characteristics of living things.

nodes.label: Vitamin
nodes.definition: A &%Nutrient present in natural products or made synthetically, which is essential in the diet of &%Humans and other higher &%Animals. Included here are &%Vitamin precursors and provitamins.

nodes.label: War
nodes.definition: A military confrontation between two or more &%GeopoliticalAreas or &%Organizations whose members are &%GeopoliticalAreas. As the corresponding axiom specifies, a &%War is made up of &%Battles.

nodes.label: Water
nodes.definition: The &%Class of samples of the compound H20. Note that this &%Class covers both pure and impure &%Water.

nodes.label: Water Area
nodes.definition: A body which is made up predominantly of water, e.g. rivers, lakes, oceans, etc.

nodes.label: Weapon
nodes.definition: The &%Class of &%Devices that are designed primarily to damage or destroy &%Humans/&%Animals, &%StationaryArtifacts or the places inhabited by &%Humans/&%Animals.

nodes.label: Word
nodes.definition: A term of a &%Language that represents a concept.
